nodes.source_text: The OER activity was assessed by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) in 1.0 M KOH at room temperature. LSV curves were treated with geometric area normalization and 90%-iR compensation unless indicated otherwise... Mo-CoN exhibits a better OER activity with an overpotential of 197 mV at 10 mA cm^{-2}... To reach 100 and 300 mA·cm^{-2}, Mo-CoN needs the overpotentials as low as 317 and 356 mV... Mo-CoN possesses a smaller Tafel slope of 78.6 mV dec^{-1}... The charge transfer resistances (R_ct) of 1.6 Ω for Mo-CoN... Mo-CoN has a larger electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) with a double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of 11.69 mF cm^{-2}... We performed continuous OER operation at 50 mA cm^{-2} and gained the current decays of 11% after 100 h for Mo-CoN
CoN (279 mV)... The charge transfer resistances (R_ct) of ... 3.9 Ω for CoN... CoN has significant current decreases of 32% after 23 h under the same condition.
Co(OH)₂ (335 mV)... The charge transfer resistances (R_ct) of ... 5.1 Ω for Co(OH)₂

Mo-CoN has an overpotential of 97 mV at 10 mA cm^{-2}... The overpotential difference of Mo-CoN between 100 and 300 mA cm^{-2} is only 15 mV... The Tafel slope of Mo-CoN (105.6 mV dec^{-1})... Mo-CoN displays a slight decay of 8% after 135 h at -50 mA cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of CoN and Mo-CoN show diffraction peaks indexed to (111), (200), and (220) planes of CoN. Mo-CoN shows a 0.32° shift toward low angles with inter-planar distances of 0.248 nm vs 0.246 nm for CoN, indicating 0.88% tensile lattice strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of CoN and Mo-CoN show three strong diffraction peaks of metallic Ni from NF (Figure 1a). The diffraction peaks of Mo-CoN are indexed to the (111), (200), and (220) planes of CoN. Mo-CoN inherits the XRD characteristics of pristine CoN with a shift of 0.32° toward low angles...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show three peaks at 646.9, 505.8, and 457.3 cm⁻¹ assigned to A₁g, F₂g, and E_g vibration modes of CoN in Mo-CoN, undergoing blue shift relative to CoN, indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1c shows three Raman peaks at 646.9, 505.8, and 457.3 cm⁻¹, respectively, which are assigned to the A₁g, F₂g, and E_g vibration modes of CoN. These peaks undergo a blue shift relative to those of CoN...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows well-aligned dense nanosheets with wrinkle shape and interconnected feature for Mo-CoN, inheriting the same morphology as CoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The panoramic views of Mo-CoN at different magnifications show well-aligned and dense nanosheets with a wrinkle shape and an interconnected feature (Figure 1d,e; Figure S2, Supporting Information)...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanosheet feature of Mo-CoN. HRTEM reveals lattice distance of 0.251 nm for (111) plane of Mo-CoN vs 0.247 nm for CoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image in Figure 1f shows the nanosheet feature and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Figure 1g shows a lattice distance of Mo-CoN (0.251 nm) for the (111) plane of CoN...

nodes.characterization_summary: GPA images display tensile strain distribution across ε_xx and ε_yy for Mo-CoN, while CoN shows almost no lattice strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: GPA images display that Mo-CoN shows a distribution composed of tensile strain across ε_xx and ε_yy, and CoN almost has no lattice strain (Figure 1h,j).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES reveals 8.1 wt.% Mo content in Mo-CoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) analyses the Mo content and reveals 8.1 wt.% Mo in the Mo-CoN.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Co 2p spectrum shows Co²⁺ (Co-O) and Co³⁺ (Co-N) peaks with slight negative shift in Mo-CoN compared to CoN. Mo 3d peaks at 232.38 eV and 235.51 eV confirm high-valence Mo⁶⁺. N 1s peak at 398.49 eV for M-N bonds shows negative shift with Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p spectrum can be deconvoluted to Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂ with two satellite peaks (identified as 'Sat.'), corresponding to Co²⁺ (Co-O) and Co³⁺ (Co-N) (Figure 2a). The high-resolution Mo 3d spectrum is assigned to Mo 3d₅/₂ and Mo 3d₃/₂ at 232.38 and 235.51 eV, proving high-valence Mo⁶⁺ in Mo-CoN (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows similar absorption edges for Mo-CoN and CoN. Mo K-edge XANES of Mo-CoN is close to MoO₃, confirming +6 oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge Xray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra present that both the absorption edges of Mo-CoN and CoN are almost the same... The Mo K-edge XANES spectra display that the absorption edge of Mo-CoN is higher than that of Mo foil and MoO₂ and is close to that of MoO₃...

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Co-Co at 2.55 Å and Co-N at 2.12 Å for Mo-CoN vs 2.53 Å and 2.10 Å for CoN (0.95% lattice expansion). Mo K-edge shows Mo-Mo at 2.76 Å and Mo-N at 2.44 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS curve of Mo-CoN shows significant peaks at 2.55 and 2.12 Å which are attributed to the Co-Co and Co-N coordinations (Figure 2e). The EXAFS peaks of CoN are located on the left side of Mo-CoN (2.53 and 2.10 Å)...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman under applied potentials shows transformation from CoN to CoOOH starting at 1.2 V with peaks at 467 and 552 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the bias voltage gradually increasing, structure transformation starts from 1.2 V with two peaks appearing at 467 and 552 cm⁻¹ for the E_g bending and A₁g stretching vibration modes of CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES analysis shows lower Co dissolution from Mo-CoN solutions compared to CoN after OER stability tests at 50 and 500 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES was further used to analyze the dissolution of Co during OER. The Co contents of the solutions after OER stability tests at 50 and 500 mA cm⁻² for CoN and Mo-CoN were determined (Table S4, Supporting Information).
